correctness.rationale: The central nonscalar-compression lemma is checked directly: take x,y with Ax,Ay independent and a bounded V with VAU=I2. If all admissible VBU are scalar, varying V by coordinate functionals vanishing on ran(AU) forces Bx,By to lie in span(Ax,Ay), and their scalar compression makes both Bx=cAx and By=cAy. Varying x,y with overlapping pairs yields one c globally; for any z in ker A, compare x+z and x, giving Bz=0. Thus B=cA contradicts independence. For a nonscalar 2x2 M, choose an explicit traceless involution H with tr(HM)!=0, then T=UHV has rank2. PQ/QP yields the nonzero spectrum of H(λI+µM), with trace µtr(HM)!=0 if µ!=0 and eigenvalues ±λ if µ=0. This proves strict positivity, uniform over the compact parameter sphere. Rank-one T gives a nonzero C in trace-kernel of V, making CT²=0; if all C rank<=1 the same holds for any T. Independently exhaustively tested the H matrix identities for 78 small-entry nonscalar matrices. Verified finite tests are not proof of the Banach-space lemma.
